Smtp.//: Every outbound email is sent from FromAddress via this account, regardless of caller. Blank Host falls back to logging-only (see DependencyInjection.AddInfrastructure).

Auth.//RequireEmailVerification: §9.34. Turn this on in the same change that wires a real email provider — with the logging-only INotificationService it would lock every new customer out until an operator read the server log.

Notifications.//SweepIntervalMinutes: §9.36. How often the lifecycle worker runs. 0 disables it entirely.

Platform.//PublicBaseUrl: The FRONTEND's own address (Shop/BackOffice/SuperOffice, whichever renders the page) - the last-resort default for customer-facing page links (email verification, password reset, unsubscribe). A caller that knows its own origin should send it as RedirectBaseUrl on the request instead (see AllowedFrontendOrigins/Business.CustomDomain) - this is only what's used when that isn't supplied, doesn't validate, or isn't available.
Platform.//ApiBaseUrl: This API's OWN address - used only to resolve a Business's relative LogoUrl to an absolute URL for outbound email. Prefers the live request's own host when one is in flight (a dev tunnel, production - no config needed); this value is only the fallback for the one code path with no request to read, the lifecycle sweep background worker.
Platform.//AllowedFrontendOrigins: Known-legitimate frontends for the BackOffice/SuperOffice/Platform realm (no Business to check a CustomDomain against) - same shape as Cors:AllowedOrigins. A request's RedirectBaseUrl (e.g. window.location.origin) is only ever honored if it exactly matches an entry here; otherwise PublicBaseUrl is used. Lets several distinct frontend deployments (staging, prod, a white-label instance) share this one backend correctly, without ever trusting an unvalidated client-supplied redirect on a password-reset email.
